I have been playing FM since I can't remember! I love this game in general.. with good or bad releases, I don't really care. What I care about is that you guys are listening to your community and yet again we have a massive upgrade to the last game in the face of FM 27! Thanks for listening <3 Let the tactical struggle begin!

Finally a decent FM game. This one feels a step in the right direction but still not up to the level of 23/24.
These are the positive/negative points I found after a full season played.

+ Improvements to UI but not perfect, skin download can help with this problem.
+ Tactical focus/effectiveness very important, so no plug & play tactics anymore.
+ Training much more important thanks to the tactical focus.

- Optimization not good for a mostly data driven game, locking fps to 30/60 is worse than "automatic".
- Audio, no volume sliders and crowd delay? sometimes the crowd reacts a second or 2 later after a goal.
- Match engine (at this point, update later this month) is not good, defending is terrible, especially wingbacks. Offensive crosses all the way.
- Instant result almost always is better than "managing" the match yourself.
- Tactical effectiveness good, players forgetting how to play it after 2 weeks no focus on it or break not.
- Kits clashing, many times both teams have blue kits(in my save) with almost no difference in blue color and if you're lucky 1 of the teams has black shorts.
Big improvement on 26, much more playable, the game has got harder, but so much better.
The last one I played was FM24, and it feels like I have to learn Football Manager all over again, just like back in 2005!

This game is a definite step in the right direction. They fixed 95% of the flaws of fm26 and added some nice new features like tactical effectiveness. Some bugs still exist and some polishing is definitely required, but from what I understand, these problems will be fixed in the upcoming update (pretty weird that they couldn't do it for the day 1 update though). All in all, this is still easily the best football management game on the market and I feel like this is a game I can put hundreds of hours into again
Sports Interactive has learned from the previous title. I enjoyed the news in FM26. But this feels more polished. Well done!

Have been playing since fm23 and while I liked the game there were a couple of features that I cant find from fm24, can't check the average age from my team from the squad planning report like in fm24 and can't create edit views.

Now this feels like Football Manager again! It is better than Football Manager 2026 in everyway possible!
Much better interface than 26, but it was very much the game that should have been 26 not 27. Still, it’s fun and challenging this year.

Unlike FM26, the return of cup draws and Transfer Deadline Day really brings back that classic Football Manager excitement.

The interface is much more detailed, and the ability to directly influence what happens on the pitch puts FM27 a step ahead of its predecessors. However, after 50 hours of gameplay, I still haven't come across any social media reactions. I genuinely miss those messages. Some of them used to really fire me up.

On the other hand, watching my defenders stand around and admire the ball while my striker sends every shot straight into the stands provides an incredibly realistic football experience. But hey, I love my boys no matter what.

There's definitely room for improvement, and I'm confident the game will get even better. But honestly, even in its current state, FM27 is a fantastic game.

The most important impression is simple: this is Football Manager once again. The immersion is back, the game runs much more smoothly and the UI is back to being logical and understandable. The Tactical Effectiveness and Tactical Tweaks are not huge changes, but they feel significant enough still. Yes, this feels more like a comprehensive bug fix rather than a new version, but this was somewhat expected after last year. I can live with that - the game is still an upgrade over FM24 due to IP/OOP, Effectiveness, DoF role and other tweaks, and naturally a huge upgrade over FM26.

Thank you for coming back SI, and thank you for bringing us back. I'm sold.
This is a real return to form from FM. Match engine looks better, game runs smoother, UI is clearly improved and I'm having a great time with my Blackburn save.
It's not perfect, but if want your Football Manager fix again then this is finally a really solid product after the debacle of 26.

FM 26 Pro Max, now with a broken Match Engine, and a RNG micromanagement side quest called Tactical Effectiveness. On top of the usual horrible squad building logic from the CPU AI, it also can't handle the new effectiveness system... Another year of having to wait for patches to incrementally fix thing, and needing a plethora of mods to make the game enjoyable in the long run.

Unless you enjoy your fullbacks escorting the opponent's wingers right next to your box, centrebacks being oblivious to defensive positioning during crosses, strikers not knowing what an offside is, or your whole squad learning your tactics at a snail's pace... EZ skip for now.

Played around 25 hours in the pre-launch (launch was just today) and looking forward to continuing my journey. I feel like them magic really is back. The UI is about a million times better, the flow of the game is widly improved. I played hundreds and hundreds of hours of FM until '26 when I bounced off despite really trying - and I am already back in and hooked. So happy to have my FM back!!

Imperfections? Sure. For me, the defensive behaviour is a bit head-scratching at time (very high level, elite, fast defenders seemingly unable to track a run, as an example) and the behaviour of wing-backs seemingly only EVER turning back at the byline and never crossing (as another example) are examples of what's annoying me. But the first post-release patch is meant to target some of these things. 

The game is also far, far harder than previous iterations, IMHO. But some of that I suspect is getting to used to the new additions (like tactical effectiveness) and I fully welcome it. 

An awesome game that will only get better with time.

At first, I hated the game. I set up my usual tactics and it was horrible. I was one of the top teams in a 2 horse race league but I was dropping points constantly. I started paying a lot more attention to my training and tactical effectiveness and after some trial and error I slowly started seeing improvements. I manage to guide my team to a hard fought league title on the last day. The game isn't a case of picking a meta tactic and storm the league, its more detailed which is great once to get the hang of it. I'm still getting the hang of the new tactic over haul but its a breath of fresh air and makes the game a lot more detailed tactically and a lot harder in a good way. My only criticism is that the AI tactics can feel over powered for teams but overall I am really enjoying it....for now (fresh off a league and cup double)

As usual for me, you can safely ignore the reviews if you want. There is a demo available for download on the store page. It is the full game but limited to six months of in-game time. That is more than enough time to decide if the game is for you.

As for me, I have no reservations about recommending the game to others because... Yeah baby, Football Manager is back!
Finally a real experience that was intended for FM26 with additional content. Even if I still prefer the old UI with side buttons, this one is quite alright.

While not a total sweat like some of these people with 1000's of hours in the game, I typically get in a couple hundred hours each year, primarily focused on lower league football. 26 was a struggle. I can appreciate what they were trying for, but it came out half cooked and I never really got into it. 27..... feels like FM again. I even appreciate the added difficulty of tactical familiarity. If you are on the fence, get the game, it mostly feels like old FM with a better more updated interface. Now if they could just do something about Newgen faces....
